title: [Chinese Subtitled Dubbing] CLO Official Tutorial Video ~ Quick Start Guide
description:
【Teaching Materials Available on WeChat Official Account】The official Chinese-dubbed teaching videos with subtitles are finally here~~~!!! Don’t wait any longer, join us and start learning now!  
You are just one step away from becoming a CLO master~  
Follow our WeChat official account CLO3D and reply with “practice files” to receive the official CLO Chinese teaching videos along with the corresponding practice files.
transcript:
In the upper left corner of the interface, the main menu is displayed.  
The upper right corner shows the user name.  
Next to it is a different mode selection.  
Click on the triangle next to "Simulation."  
Here you can see different modes.  
In Simulation mode, simulate 3D clothing.  
In Animation mode, perform embroidery animation.  
In Cherry Blossom Placement mode, determine the placement of the positioning flower.  
In Color Scheme, complete multi-color design.  
In Backup mode, you can create backups, which is convenient for communication between departments.  
In Fabric Calculation mode, use fabric measurement to convert measured fabric data into electronic fabric data.  
In Modelization mode, you can create models.  
In Material List mode, you can type out the price list.  

On the left side of the page is the drawing window.  
Here you can open and use the default folder provided by CLO.  
In the upper right corner of the drawing window, there are three buttons.  
The first button is the download button.  
When you need to update and download, click the download button to update and download.  
The second button is the increase button.  
Click on the increase button to add the practice file to the drawing window.  
In the drop-down menu, you can store instructions.  
Click the upright button the first time.  
On the right side of the drawing window, you can align the cloth categories.  
Click on the shaking button.  
The last one is the reset button.  

On the right side of the 3D window, you can create and edit 2D versions.  
In the upper right corner of the page is the object window.  
Here all elements related to 3D clothing are displayed.  
Below the object window is the attribute editor.  
Here you can check or edit the attributes of the selected object.  

There are three buttons in the lower right corner of the page.  
The middle button only shows the 3D window, not the 2D window.  
The right button only shows the 2D window, not the 3D window.  
If you need both windows to display simultaneously, click the button on the left to display the 2D and 3D windows at the same time.  

Double-click to open the Produce Files folder in the library window, find Quickstart, then open 2ViewControl.  
Double-click on ViewControl, or drag it to the 3D window.  
The 2D window is similar to the 3D window.  
First, place the mouse in the 3D window, roll the wheel to zoom in or zoom out the 3D image.  
Scroll the wheel in the opposite direction, move the mouse to the 2D window, roll the wheel to zoom in or zoom out the 2D image.  
Move the mouse to the 3D window, press the scroll button and move the mouse to zoom in or out the 3D image.  
Scroll the wheel, move the mouse to the 2D window, press the scroll button and move the mouse to zoom in or out the 2D image.  
Move the mouse to the 3D window, press the right mouse button and move the mouse to zoom in or out the 3D image.  
Since the 2D window is a flat window, you cannot perform three-dimensional inspection there.  

In the 3D window's blank keypad area, the upper half of the menu bar is the view menu.  
There are options for front, back, left, right, etc.  
Next to them are their shortcuts.  
Remember that these shortcuts work more effectively.  
Transfer the view using the keyboard.  
Imagine the model is in position 5.  
2 is front, 8 is back, 4 is right, 6 is left, 5 is top, 0 is top.  

Now back to the 2D view.  
Double-click to open the Produce Files folder in the 3D window.  
Find Quickstart.  
Then open 3Simulation.  
Double-click on the Simulation file or drag it to the 3D window.  
Open the first tool in the 3D toolbar, the simulation tool.  
You can see the 3D window fabric falling to the ground.  
This is because after opening the simulation, the fabric starts simulating using the gravity system in the 3D window.  

Next to the simulation, there is a cursor.  
This is the selection tool.  
Use the selection tool to left-click on the 3D window panel and move the mouse.  
The panel moves like real fabric.  
Close the simulation.  
The selection tool’s cursor becomes a cursor made up of an arrow and a cross.  
Close the simulation.  
Use the selection tool to left-click on the 3D window panel and move the mouse.  
The panel moves like real fabric.  
This is because after closing the simulation, the gravity system stops calculating.  

Double-click to open the Produce Files folder in the 2D window.  
Find Quickstart.  
Then open 4Simulation.  
Drag it to the 3D window or double-click on the document arrangement.  
On the 3D window panel, the left button will pop up a positioning ball made up of three pull rods and three arcs.  
Pull the red pull rod to move the panel left and right on the screen.  
Pull the green pull rod to move the panel up and down on the screen.  
Pull the blue pull rod to move the panel closer or farther away from you.  
The yellow small square is more convenient to move the panel horizontally and vertically.  

Place the mouse in the green circle, press the left button and move the mouse.  
You can see the panel rotating around the outer axis, turning left and right.  
Place the mouse in the blue circle, press the left button and move the mouse.  
You can see the panel rotating clockwise or counterclockwise.  

Use the positioning tool to arrange the front panel around the model.  
You can see the panel moving left and right on the screen.  
Move the reference to an accordion and then release the thumb of the ruler again.  
Press the right button and move it along the horizontal axis, rotating right and left relative to the model.  

Using screen coordinates means using the x and y axes of the camera as the coordinates.  
The selected object moves along the camera’s axis.  
In the 3D window, right-click to open the menu, select Coordinates.  
You can see there are three types of coordinates.  
Currently, I’m using screen coordinates.  
Change it to horizontal coordinates.  
Horizontal coordinate positioning ball is aligned according to the orientation of the object itself.  
Mainly used when designing actions on the x and y joints of the virtual model.  
The selected object moves along the orientation of the object itself.  

In the 3D window, right-click to open the menu, select Coordinates.  
You can see there are three types of coordinates.  
World coordinates use the three-dimensional basic axes as the positioning ball’s axis.  
It is unrelated to the screen or the object.  

In the 3D window, select the front panel.  
Pull the red lever.  
You can see the three-dimensional spatial axes.  
You can see that the board moves left and right on the screen and the model.  
Select the side angle of the channel and pull the red lever again.  
The board still moves left and right on the model and does not change axis with camera movement.  
The selected object uses the basic three-dimensional spatial axis as its movement axis.  
It has no relation to the screen or object orientation.  

In the 3D blank area, right-click and adjust the coordinates from world coordinates to screen coordinates.  
Use the positioning tool to move the board to the model.  
However, you can use the arrangement points to make this faster and more convenient.  

Select the mouse in the fourth position in the 3D vertical toolbar.  
Select the second one.  
Use the positioning tool to select the display arrangement points.  
Blue dots will appear around the virtual model.  
These are the arrangement points.  

Right-click on the front panel in the 3D window.  
Move the mouse to the arrangement point.  
You can see that the arrangement points will appear as a gray preview.  
After selecting the arrangement point, right-click on the blue arrangement point.  
You can see that the panel is arranged to the arrangement point.  
The panel is curved and wrapped around the virtual model.  

Scroll down the attribute editor and find Arrangement.  
In the Arrangement purple bar, there are several options such as X-axis, Y-axis, and Z-axis.  
The X-axis is the horizontal movement relative to the human body.  
The Y-axis is the vertical movement along the body.  
The Z-axis is the distance between the panel and the body.  
If there is a problem with the arrangement position, you can adjust the panel’s position by modifying these data.  

In the 3D window, right-click on the left and select the sleeve panel.  
Move the mouse to the sleeve’s arrangement point.  
Right-click on the arrangement point.  
Place the sleeve panel down.  
Rotate the view to the back view or press shortcut key 8.  
Right-click on the back panel.  
Right-click on the arrangement point.  
Place the back panel down.  
Rotate the view to the front view.  
Select shortcut key 2.  

Move the mouse to the fourth tool in the vertical toolbar.  
Select the second-level tool.  
Show the arrangement points.  
Hide the arrangement points.  

Open the Practice Files folder in the drawing window.  
Find Quickstart.  
Then open 5.Sewing.  
Click on the Sewing file or drag it to the 3D window.  
If you need to join two panels, you need to use sewing lines to sew them together.  

In the 2D toolbar, find the line sewing tool.  
Sew line by line.  
Press two lines to complete a pair of sewing lines.  
You can see two cutouts on the sewing line.  
This shows the sewing line’s direction.  
When sewing, make sure the sewing lines are in the same direction.  
If the sewing lines are opposite, it will cause the 3D clothing to twist and be unstable.  

You can use the edge sewing tool.  
On the wrong sewing line, right-click.  
In the cutout menu, select Swap Sewing Line.  
Select the area where the leading edge sewing line has been cut out.  
Here you can see the 3D cutout is now clear.  

You can also delete the wrong sewing line and resew.  
In addition to sewing in the 2D window, you can also sew in the 3D window.  
Select the line sewing tool, press two lines separately in the 3D window to create a pair of sewing lines.  

On the third set of lines, you can see many dots that have broken the line.  
If you continue to use the line sewing here, you will find the distance between lines is inconsistent.  
Here you need to use the free sewing tool.  

In the 2D toolbar, find the free sewing tool.  
On the starting point of the panel, press the left button, slide the mouse to the end, and press again to complete the first sewing step.  
On the starting point of another line, press the left button, slide to the end, and press again to complete sewing.  
Four presses in total create a pair of sewing lines.  

When using free sewing, pay attention to the direction of the sewing line.  
Similarly, you can also use free sewing in the 3D window.  
At the starting point, press the left button; at the end point, click twice to complete.  
Use the same method on the other line to complete a pair of sewing lines.  

When sewing multiple lines, you cannot use only line sewing or free sewing here.  
On the line sewing tool, left-click and hold.  
In the toolbar, select M-N line sewing.  
On the panel, click the line corresponding to the M section.  
Press the Return key to complete the selection of M section.  
Click the sewing line corresponding to the N section.  
Press the Return key to complete the line sewing of the N section.  

When sewing, also pay attention to the direction of the sewing line to keep it consistent.  
When there are many points on multiple lines and the line is broken, use M-N free sewing.  

On the free sewing tool, left-click and hold.  
In the menu bar, select M-N free sewing.  
On the outside of the panel, click the M section sewing.  
Press the Return key to complete the selection of M section sewing.  
Repeat the same operation for N section sewing.  
Complete M-N sewing.  
Pay attention to the sewing line direction.  

After completing M section sewing, open the simulation.  
The panel in the 3D window will merge together.  

Double-click to open the Produce Files folder in the picture window.  
Find Quickstart.  
Then open 6.Garment.  
Double-click on the dress document or drag it to the 3D window.  
Drag it to the 3D window.  
Unscrew the contrast light.  
Press OK.  
Download the version to the cloud.  
Unscrew the contrast light.  

Open the FV2 FFA file, double-click or drag it to the 3D window.  
Since there is only half of the panel, you need to align the other half.  
Use the edit panel tool in the 2D window.  
Right-click on the front middle line.  
In the menu bar, select Align to open the edit line.  
The aligned panel will be shown in blue.  
When selecting a line or point on either side, the corresponding line or point on the other side will also show bright blue, indicating a link between them.  

When the panel is aligned, editing one side will also edit the other side and the lines between the aligned panels simultaneously.  
Similarly, right-click on the back middle line.  
In the menu bar, select Align to open the edit line.  
The other half will be aligned.  

After aligning the panels, select Rearrange All 2D Arrangement Positions in the 3D window.  
Align the 2D arrangement to the 3D window.  
Open the 3D model arrangement points.  
Parts of the arrangement points may be blocked.  
You can select all panels in the 2D window.  
Press Ctrl-A to select all panels.  
Move the panels up and out of the blocked arrangement points.  
Click left-click to cancel selection.  

Click left-click on the front panel.  
Move the mouse to the arrangement point.  
Click left-click to place the front panel on the model.  
You can see some panels have been moved to the model.  
The panel has been moved onto the model’s body.  

In the property editor, drag to the bottom.  
In the Arrangement purple bar, enlarge the radius.  
Press Ctrl-A to rotate the view to the back view.  
Click on the back panel.  
Click on the model arrangement point.  
Place the panel down.  
You can also adjust the value in the Arrangement purple bar in the property editor.  

Use the line sewing tool to sew the panels.  
When sewing, pay attention to the sewing line direction.  
Sew the side seams using line sewing.  
Press two lines separately to create a pair of sewing lines.  
Because it is a joint panel, only half of the sewing is needed.  
The other half will automatically match the sewing line.  

When sewing the shoulder line, click near the shoulder line point.  
Then click at the surface point.  
Click again at the back tied point.  
In the finished left-line sewing, be careful with the sewing line direction.  

After finishing the simulation, the panel naturally rests on the virtual model.  
The typical pose of the virtual model with both hands open is used to wear clothes conveniently.  
When the 3D costume is worn on the virtual model or platform, the model’s posture is adjusted to a straight posture to check body balance.  

In the walkthrough window, double-click to open the Avid folder, find FemaleVR, and find the Pose file.  
Double-click FV203 or drag it to the 3D window.  
Play the pose and click OK.  
Adjust the model’s posture to a straight posture.  

Use the editor version tool.  
On the front collar, front sleeve, back collar, and back sleeve, click on the left shoulder.  
At the top of the model editor, you can see the 2D line section and the 3D line section.  
You can find these two lines.  
The difference between the two values is relatively large.  
This is due to the weight of the costume and deformation caused.  

In the 2D toolbar, select the stitch tool.  
Single-click on the collar and sleeve to apply the stitch.  
The stitch tool is selected.  
In the element editor, find the stitch line.  
Here you can change the width of the stitch line.  
In the preview, you can adjust the stitch type.  

Open the simulation and apply the stitch to the 3D costume.  
You can see the collar and sleeve stretch.  
To check if the dress is correct, the 3D costume’s shoulder line needs to match the virtual model’s shoulder line.  

From the 3D toolbar, select the virtual model strap tool.  
On the virtual model, single-click the left mouse button to create the start point.  
Double-click the left mouse button to create the end point.  
You can add another virtual model strap.  

Use the attach to virtual model strap tool.  
First, click on the 3D costume shoulder line.  
Then click on the corresponding virtual model strap.  
Open the simulation, attach the 3D costume strap to the virtual model strap.  
Click OK.  
Close the simulation.  

Open the library window and find Fabric.  
There are more than 70 fabric types provided by the system.  
Find Knit Cotton Jersey and drag it to the Fabric window.  
Open the model; the clothing simulates the correct shape according to the properties of the selected fabric.  

Drag a JPG image from the File Manager to the Fabric window.  
The fabric is applied to the fabric and displayed on the 3D clothing.  

In the 2D window toolbar, select the Edit Fabric Tool.  
On any panel, left-click to see a double arrow direction indicator.  
Place the mouse in the middle and press the mouse to move the fabric position.  
Press and move the mouse to reposition the fabric.  
Place the mouse on either end.  
Press Shift to rotate the fabric.  
You can feel a curtain effect.  
This is a 45-degree or 90-degree rotation of the fabric pattern.  
This changes the fabric pattern direction on the panel, not the fabric grain direction.  

In the 2D window, the top right corner of the panel has a 3D curtain and a round-shoulder-shaped fabric editor.  
The curtain can be enlarged or reduced.  
The round-shoulder-shaped movement can rotate the fabric.  
Press Shift here to apply a 45° or 90° rotation.  
Here, we are changing the pattern direction of the fabric, not the weave direction of the panel.  

To improve clothing realism, in the 3D toolbar, choose the tool to improve clothing quality.  
You can reduce the particle diameter with one click,  
read the panel thickness,  
and measure the surface diameter of the model.  
Select the pattern direction and click OK.  
Activate the simulation and apply the settings to the 3D clothing.  
You can see the clothing detail has changed.  

Here, the simulation speed is relatively slow, and it is not recommended to modify the clothing afterward.  
Click OK.  

After completion, save the file as a project in the main menu.  
When saving the file, the file name cannot contain Chinese characters or special symbols, but can only contain letters, numbers, or lowercase letters.  

Let’s try to change the lighting of the model.  
Click OK.  
In the 3D model, this screen appears with the 3D aspect ratio and background color.  
For each photo,  
you can change the angle,  
speed,  
or position of the screen.  
This is the 3D model view.  
Add this and this.  
Now, you can change the lighting of the model.  
You can change the 3D view of the model.  
Click OK.  
The button will pop up.  
Click OK.  
You can see there are three colors in the model.

chunks.content: # CLO Official Tutorial Video: Quick Start Guide This document provides a detailed guide to the CLO 3D garment design software interface, tools, and workflow. It covers mode selections, window layouts, 2D and 3D navigation, coordinate systems, garment arrangement, sewing techniques, fabric application, stitching, and simulation settings to assist users in effectively creating and editing virtual garments. --- ## Interface Overview and Mode Selection This section explains the main interface components, mode selections, and their functions, including simulation, animation, fabric calculation, and backup options. - **Main Menu**: Located at the upper left corner. - **User Name and Mode Selection**: Upper right corner displays the username and a dropdown next to "Simulation" for mode switching. - **Available Modes**: - **Simulation Mode**: Simulate 3D clothing under gravity. - **Animation Mode**: Perform embroidery animations. - **Cherry Blossom Placement Mode**: Determine positioning flower placement. - **Color Scheme Mode**: Complete multi-color designs. - **Backup Mode**: Create backups for cross-department communication. - **Fabric Calculation Mode**: Convert measured fabric data into electronic fabric data. - **Modelization Mode**: Create 3D models. - **Material List Mode**: Generate price lists. --- ## Window Layout and Navigation Tools This section details the layout of drawing, 2D, and 3D windows, along with navigation tools and controls for manipulating views and objects. - **Drawing Window (Left Side)**: - Default folder access. - Three buttons at the upper right: Download (update files), Increase (add practice files), and Reset. - Cloth category alignment button ("shaking button"). - **3D Window (Right Side)**: - Create and edit 2D versions here. - Object window (upper right) lists all 3D clothing elements. - Attribute editor (below object window) for checking and editing selected object attributes. - View display buttons at lower right: - Middle: Show only 3D window. - Right: Show only 2D window. - Left: Show both 2D and 3D windows simultaneously. - **Zooming and Panning**: - Mouse wheel to zoom in/out in both 2D and 3D windows. - Press scroll button and drag to pan. - Right mouse button drag to zoom in/out in 3D. - 2D window is flat; no 3D inspection possible. - **View Menu and Shortcuts in 3D Window**: - Options for front, back, left, right, top views. - Numeric keypad shortcuts for views: - 2: Front - 8: Back - 4: Right - 6: Left - 5 / 0: Top --- ## Using Simulation and Selection Tools This section covers how to start/stop simulation, use selection and positioning tools, and manipulate garment panels in 3D space. - **Opening Simulation**: - Open simulation tool from the 3D toolbar. - Fabric simulates gravity, falling naturally. - **Selection Tool**: - Cursor changes between simulation active and inactive. - Move panels by left-click dragging; behaves like real fabric when simulation is off. - **Positioning Tool**: - Activated via practice files (e.g., 4Simulation). - Positioning ball with three pull rods (red, green, blue) and arcs: - Red: Move panel left/right. - Green: Move panel up/down. - Blue: Move panel closer/farther. - Yellow square for horizontal and vertical movement.

chunks.content: - Fabric simulates gravity, falling naturally. - **Selection Tool**: - Cursor changes between simulation active and inactive. - Move panels by left-click dragging; behaves like real fabric when simulation is off. - **Positioning Tool**: - Activated via practice files (e.g., 4Simulation). - Positioning ball with three pull rods (red, green, blue) and arcs: - Red: Move panel left/right. - Green: Move panel up/down. - Blue: Move panel closer/farther. - Yellow square for horizontal and vertical movement. - Rotations: - Green circle: Rotate left/right. - Blue circle: Rotate clockwise/counterclockwise. - Used to arrange panels precisely around the virtual model. --- ## Coordinate Systems in 3D Window Understanding coordinate types is essential for precise garment manipulation. - **Coordinate Types** (Accessed via right-click menu > Coordinates): - **Screen Coordinates**: Movement along the camera’s x and y axes. - **Horizontal Coordinates**: Aligned with the object's own orientation; used for joint movement design. - **World Coordinates**: Fixed three-dimensional axes independent of screen or object orientation. - **Examples**: - Moving the front panel with red lever shows three-dimensional spatial axes. - Switching between coordinate types changes how objects move relative to the camera and model. --- ## Arrangement Points and Panel Positioning This section explains how to use arrangement points to fit garment panels onto the virtual model accurately. - **Displaying Arrangement Points**: - Use the fourth tool in the 3D vertical toolbar, second-level tool. - Blue dots appear around the virtual model indicating arrangement points. - **Using Arrangement Points**: - Right-click on a panel, hover over an arrangement point to preview. - Select a blue arrangement point to snap the panel onto the model. - The panel bends and wraps naturally around the model’s body. - **Attribute Editor Adjustments**: - In the Arrangement section, adjust: - X-axis: Horizontal movement relative to the body. - Y-axis: Vertical movement along the body. - Z-axis: Distance from the panel to the body. - Adjust these values to correct panel positioning if necessary. - **Practical Use**: - Apply arrangement points to sleeves, back panels, and other parts. - Rotate views to align panels accurately. --- ## Sewing Techniques: Line, Free, and M-N Sewing This section covers sewing tools and best practices for joining garment panels in 2D and 3D windows. - **Line Sewing Tool**: - Click two corresponding lines to create sewing lines. - Sewing lines have directional cutouts; direction must be consistent to avoid twisting. - Wrong sewing direction can be corrected by right-clicking and selecting “Swap Sewing Line.” - Sewing can be done in both 2D and 3D windows. - **Free Sewing Tool**: - Used when line distances are inconsistent or lines are broken. - Click and drag from start to end points on each panel to create sewing lines. - Direction consistency remains critical. - Free sewing also available in 3D window. - **M-N Sewing** (for multiple lines): - Accessed by left-click and holding the line sewing or free sewing tool. - Select M section line(s), press Return. - Select N section line(s), press Return.

chunks.content: - **Free Sewing Tool**: - Used when line distances are inconsistent or lines are broken. - Click and drag from start to end points on each panel to create sewing lines. - Direction consistency remains critical. - Free sewing also available in 3D window. - **M-N Sewing** (for multiple lines): - Accessed by left-click and holding the line sewing or free sewing tool. - Select M section line(s), press Return. - Select N section line(s), press Return. - Completes multiple line sewing simultaneously. - Direction consistency must be maintained. - **Simulation After Sewing**: - Open simulation to see panels merge and behave naturally. --- ## Panel Alignment and Editing This section explains aligning garment panels symmetrically and editing linked panels. - **Opening Garment Files**: - Open files like "6.Garment" from Practice Files. - Load and unscrew contrast light for better visualization. - **Editing Panel Alignment**: - Use Edit Panel tool in 2D window. - Right-click on middle lines (front/back) and select Align. - Aligned panels turn blue; editing one side edits the symmetrical side simultaneously. - **Rearranging Panels**: - Use Rearrange All 2D Arrangement Positions to align 2D panels with 3D model. - If arrangement points are blocked, move panels up/out to clear. - Use Ctrl-A to select all panels for bulk movement. --- ## Stitching and Model Posture Adjustment This section covers applying stitches, adjusting model posture, and verifying garment fit. - **Stitch Tool**: - Select stitch tool in 2D toolbar. - Click on collar and sleeves to apply stitching. - Stitch width and type can be adjusted in the element editor. - **Model Posture**: - Typical pose: model with open hands for easy dressing. - Adjust posture to straight using pose files (e.g., FV203). - Check garment balance and fit with model in straight posture. - **Virtual Model Straps**: - Create straps by clicking start and double-clicking end point. - Attach garment shoulder lines to virtual model straps. - Attach straps via simulation to ensure fit. --- ## Fabric Application and Editing This section explains how to apply and manipulate fabric properties and textures on garment panels. - **Fabric Library**: - Over 70 fabric types available, e.g., Knit Cotton Jersey. - Drag fabric to the Fabric window to apply properties. - **Using Images as Fabric**: - Drag JPG images from File Manager to Fabric window. - Fabric texture displays on 3D garment. - **Edit Fabric Tool**: - In 2D window toolbar, select Edit Fabric Tool. - Move fabric position by dragging. - Rotate fabric patterns by pressing Shift and dragging ends. - Rotation applies to fabric pattern direction (45° or 90°), not fabric grain/weave. - **Fabric Pattern Editor**: - Located at top right of 2D panel. - Allows curtain size adjustment and fabric rotation with 45°/90° increments. --- ## Enhancing Clothing Realism and Simulation Settings This section presents tools and settings to improve garment detail and simulation quality. - **Quality Improvement Tools**: - Reduce particle diameter. - Read panel thickness. - Measure model surface diameter.

markdown_content: # CLO Official Tutorial Video: Quick Start Guide This document provides a detailed guide to the CLO 3D garment design software interface, tools, and workflow. It covers mode selections, window layouts, 2D and 3D navigation, coordinate systems, garment arrangement, sewing techniques, fabric application, stitching, and simulation settings to assist users in effectively creating and editing virtual garments. --- ## Interface Overview and Mode Selection This section explains the main interface components, mode selections, and their functions, including simulation, animation, fabric calculation, and backup options. - **Main Menu**: Located at the upper left corner. - **User Name and Mode Selection**: Upper right corner displays the username and a dropdown next to "Simulation" for mode switching. - **Available Modes**: - **Simulation Mode**: Simulate 3D clothing under gravity. - **Animation Mode**: Perform embroidery animations. - **Cherry Blossom Placement Mode**: Determine positioning flower placement. - **Color Scheme Mode**: Complete multi-color designs. - **Backup Mode**: Create backups for cross-department communication. - **Fabric Calculation Mode**: Convert measured fabric data into electronic fabric data. - **Modelization Mode**: Create 3D models. - **Material List Mode**: Generate price lists. --- ## Window Layout and Navigation Tools This section details the layout of drawing, 2D, and 3D windows, along with navigation tools and controls for manipulating views and objects. - **Drawing Window (Left Side)**: - Default folder access. - Three buttons at the upper right: Download (update files), Increase (add practice files), and Reset. - Cloth category alignment button ("shaking button"). - **3D Window (Right Side)**: - Create and edit 2D versions here. - Object window (upper right) lists all 3D clothing elements. - Attribute editor (below object window) for checking and editing selected object attributes. - View display buttons at lower right: - Middle: Show only 3D window. - Right: Show only 2D window. - Left: Show both 2D and 3D windows simultaneously. - **Zooming and Panning**: - Mouse wheel to zoom in/out in both 2D and 3D windows. - Press scroll button and drag to pan. - Right mouse button drag to zoom in/out in 3D. - 2D window is flat; no 3D inspection possible. - **View Menu and Shortcuts in 3D Window**: - Options for front, back, left, right, top views. - Numeric keypad shortcuts for views: - 2: Front - 8: Back - 4: Right - 6: Left - 5 / 0: Top --- ## Using Simulation and Selection Tools This section covers how to start/stop simulation, use selection and positioning tools, and manipulate garment panels in 3D space. - **Opening Simulation**: - Open simulation tool from the 3D toolbar. - Fabric simulates gravity, falling naturally. - **Selection Tool**: - Cursor changes between simulation active and inactive. - Move panels by left-click dragging; behaves like real fabric when simulation is off. - **Positioning Tool**: - Activated via practice files (e.g., 4Simulation). - Positioning ball with three pull rods (red, green, blue) and arcs: - Red: Move panel left/right. - Green: Move panel up/down. - Blue: Move panel closer/farther. - Yellow square for horizontal and vertical movement. - Rotations: - Green circle: Rotate left/right. - Blue circle: Rotate clockwise/counterclockwise. - Used to arrange panels precisely around the virtual model. --- ## Coordinate Systems in 3D Window Understanding coordinate types is essential for precise garment manipulation. - **Coordinate Types** (Accessed via right-click menu > Coordinates): - **Screen Coordinates**: Movement along the camera’s x and y axes. - **Horizontal Coordinates**: Aligned with the object's own orientation; used for joint movement design. - **World Coordinates**: Fixed three-dimensional axes independent of screen or object orientation. - **Examples**: - Moving the front panel with red lever shows three-dimensional spatial axes. - Switching between coordinate types changes how objects move relative to the camera and model. --- ## Arrangement Points and Panel Positioning This section explains how to use arrangement points to fit garment panels onto the virtual model accurately. - **Displaying Arrangement Points**: - Use the fourth tool in the 3D vertical toolbar, second-level tool. - Blue dots appear around the virtual model indicating arrangement points. - **Using Arrangement Points**: - Right-click on a panel, hover over an arrangement point to preview. - Select a blue arrangement point to snap the panel onto the model. - The panel bends and wraps naturally around the model’s body. - **Attribute Editor Adjustments**: - In the Arrangement section, adjust: - X-axis: Horizontal movement relative to the body. - Y-axis: Vertical movement along the body. - Z-axis: Distance from the panel to the body. - Adjust these values to correct panel positioning if necessary. - **Practical Use**: - Apply arrangement points to sleeves, back panels, and other parts. - Rotate views to align panels accurately. --- ## Sewing Techniques: Line, Free, and M-N Sewing This section covers sewing tools and best practices for joining garment panels in 2D and 3D windows. - **Line Sewing Tool**: - Click two corresponding lines to create sewing lines. - Sewing lines have directional cutouts; direction must be consistent to avoid twisting. - Wrong sewing direction can be corrected by right-clicking and selecting “Swap Sewing Line.” - Sewing can be done in both 2D and 3D windows. - **Free Sewing Tool**: - Used when line distances are inconsistent or lines are broken. - Click and drag from start to end points on each panel to create sewing lines. - Direction consistency remains critical. - Free sewing also available in 3D window. - **M-N Sewing** (for multiple lines): - Accessed by left-click and holding the line sewing or free sewing tool. - Select M section line(s), press Return. - Select N section line(s), press Return. - Completes multiple line sewing simultaneously. - Direction consistency must be maintained. - **Simulation After Sewing**: - Open simulation to see panels merge and behave naturally. --- ## Panel Alignment and Editing This section explains aligning garment panels symmetrically and editing linked panels. - **Opening Garment Files**: - Open files like "6.Garment" from Practice Files. - Load and unscrew contrast light for better visualization. - **Editing Panel Alignment**: - Use Edit Panel tool in 2D window. - Right-click on middle lines (front/back) and select Align. - Aligned panels turn blue; editing one side edits the symmetrical side simultaneously. - **Rearranging Panels**: - Use Rearrange All 2D Arrangement Positions to align 2D panels with 3D model. - If arrangement points are blocked, move panels up/out to clear. - Use Ctrl-A to select all panels for bulk movement. --- ## Stitching and Model Posture Adjustment This section covers applying stitches, adjusting model posture, and verifying garment fit. - **Stitch Tool**: - Select stitch tool in 2D toolbar. - Click on collar and sleeves to apply stitching. - Stitch width and type can be adjusted in the element editor. - **Model Posture**: - Typical pose: model with open hands for easy dressing. - Adjust posture to straight using pose files (e.g., FV203). - Check garment balance and fit with model in straight posture. - **Virtual Model Straps**: - Create straps by clicking start and double-clicking end point. - Attach garment shoulder lines to virtual model straps. - Attach straps via simulation to ensure fit. --- ## Fabric Application and Editing This section explains how to apply and manipulate fabric properties and textures on garment panels. - **Fabric Library**: - Over 70 fabric types available, e.g., Knit Cotton Jersey. - Drag fabric to the Fabric window to apply properties. - **Using Images as Fabric**: - Drag JPG images from File Manager to Fabric window. - Fabric texture displays on 3D garment. - **Edit Fabric Tool**: - In 2D window toolbar, select Edit Fabric Tool. - Move fabric position by dragging. - Rotate fabric patterns by pressing Shift and dragging ends. - Rotation applies to fabric pattern direction (45° or 90°), not fabric grain/weave. - **Fabric Pattern Editor**: - Located at top right of 2D panel. - Allows curtain size adjustment and fabric rotation with 45°/90° increments. --- ## Enhancing Clothing Realism and Simulation Settings This section presents tools and settings to improve garment detail and simulation quality. - **Quality Improvement Tools**: - Reduce particle diameter. - Read panel thickness. - Measure model surface diameter. - Choose pattern direction. - Apply settings and activate simulation to see enhanced details. -
